content:
Thinking aloud: I wonder if we should get people to answer the following question in the PR description:

“Assuming that the reviewer has access to the latest AI models, what about this PR means that it is easier for them to review then do the same task themselves?”

Ah this is good question, I was thinking of a set of questions to ask - I came up with the below and have added yours as well as point 2

  • Context: What problem or result does this PR address? How does it relate to the relevant literature or existing project work, and what gap does it fill?
  • Contribution: Suppose the reviewer could use a strong AI model to generate similar code. What project-specific or domain reasoning, design choices, or verification does this PR contribute beyond the code itself?
  • Reviewability: What would the reviewer otherwise need to reconstruct or redo to assess this PR? What have you included to make those parts straightforward to check?
  • Project fit: How does this change fit the existing API map and surrounding formalization? Does the map need updating?
Definitely not perfect but trying to organize our thinking, what do people think?

Maybe the first two could be:

1) If you were to ask someone competent in Lean, or an AI agent, to do this PR for you, what would you ask (1 sentence)?
2) Beyond this, what other input do you believe would be needed for them to get a PR of similar quality to what you have got now?
Should we make a separate thread for PR template, which I think this is what this is about

Then maybe also, for 3:
3) What have you done specific for this PR to ensure and check that the work needed for a reviewer to review this PR is minimal?

Though not sure about the best framing of all of this. It is certainly true that often a well formed single prompt to an LLM can produce a good PR and we do not want to put people off doing this.
Your questions might obtain the answer that we need but like you have mentioned I'm really stuck on the best framing
Discussion thread for the possibility of a PR template and its structure.

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

I think one extreme option to the general problem is: restrict users to at most 2 open pull requests at a time

Mhmm I wonder again if this discourages people from contributing, generally like you have mentioned its possible to get some semblance of a PR using one prompt, and I think the effort (however minimal) it takes to do this should be encouraged

Agreed

bit of a rant..

And another plus point of projects like this is that allows contributors at many levels of committment and restrictions on number of PRs might prevent this. If someone just wanted to PR and not review, should this be frowned upon? I'm not sure what the answer is but I'm leaning towards no.

What should be frowned upon is creating more work for reviewers by having fully automated PRs, we would want to encourage the use of AI as it is a transformative tool, but you must do as much due diligence as possible and answering the questions in the PR description in your own words is a minimum requirement. If this is not done then we can apply an enforcement policy?

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

Though not sure about the best framing of all of this. It is certainly true that often a well formed single prompt to an LLM can produce a good PR and we do not want to put people off doing this.

Therefore, this leads me to think, maybe the framing might be alright (even if it brings contributions down a little) provided it gets the information that helps reviewers
Bit of a tangent above, but back to the questions, what is the best way to let contributors know about this PR description template?

I agree with this. The basic thing we want is respect for each others time, both on the side of the author and on the side of the reviewer. I think part of that is good communication, and at the very least we should be communicating with authors what would make our life’s easier and hopefully the project a more pleasant place for everyone.

Yess I do think a communication deficit in the reviewers could be a part of this. We can write out this PR template on a doc and link it to agents.md so it get's surfaced through people's agents? Then we can ask some authors of current open PRs and see how this works?
I think opening a draft PR with a template might be a good start

1. What does this PR contribute, and why is it useful?

Explain the result, capability, correction, or improvement in ordinary language. For supporting mathematics, describe the physics work it enables. For a refactor, explain what becomes easier or clearer afterward.

  1. What is the physical meaning of the main definitions or results, and which assumptions or conventions matter?

Explain relevant choices about domains, regularity, dimensions, normalization, units, sign conventions, or idealizations. Where your definitions or interpretations follow the literature, link to a specific source or existing documentation.

  1. How does this build on the existing library, and why have you chosen this design?

    Point to relevant existing definitions, structures, or API-map sections. Explain significant design choices, especially where you introduce a new structure or depart from existing patterns.

  2. What is established here, and what remains assumed, deferred, or unconnected?

    Make the boundaries of your contribution clear. Distinguish assumptions from proved results, and explain any connections to physical systems that remain unfinished.

  3. How does this PR fit into the larger work, and what does it depend on?

Link relevant issues, discussions, and prerequisite PRs. If this PR is part of a stack, explain which changes belong to this PR. For foudational work, describe the applications it is intended to support.

  1. Where would you particularly like the reviewer’s attention, and what are you unsure about?

Mention specific questions about the assumptions, design, placement, or physical interpretation. For a complicated change, suggest a short reading order. You are welcome to ask for help or explain that the design is still exploratory.

Tried to adapt all of our discussions and concerns to be reflected in some way in these questions with a different style of framing. For q2 the bold part is a bit of a list that might be a bit too much, but contains all the common points I see that make reviews also slightly challenging.

Definitely lots to iterate but would like to hear what people think

Another thing working against us here is that the AGENTS.md requires descrptions to list every added or removed lemma and definition, with its file and explanation. This might explain why authors (or agents) may believe this current format is expected. It also gives agents instructions for writing descriptions

Maybe step 1 is changin this to not provide them with instructions or guides and explicitly request agents to not write PR descriptions
Yes let us make this AGENTS.md change now
Physlib#1940
Approved

I'm not sure about the questions I have provided, it invites super long PR descriptions again which lead to the same problem. Maybe we impose a line limit/word limit and then post 2-3 sharp questions to be explained in plain language

Maybe:

  1. What did you do? (1 sentence)
  2. Why did you do it? (1 sentence)
  3. How did you do it? (1 sentence)
